chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Is'haq ibn Ibrahim, from Nasr ibn Qabous, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The female singer is accursed, and accursed is the one who consumes her earnings.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the earnings of a female singer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the ruling on the female singer, declaring her accursed and extending that curse to those who consume her earnings. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the permissibility of music and the economic purity of income derived from it, linking spiritual status directly to livelihood. The emphasis on 'kasbaha' (her earnings) underscores the broader principle that the source of income can affect the spiritual state of the consumer.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashsary, from Al Hassan Biin Ali, from Is’haq Bin Ibrahim, from Nasr Bin Qabous who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The female singer is an accursed woman, and accursed is the one who consumes her earnings’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim from Nasr ibn Qabus who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
A singer female is condemned, and condemned is one who consumes the income from her singing.’”
